news.title: Key oddity of quantum physics may run even deeper than anticipated

Armstrong Roberts/ClassicStock/Getty Images Quantum mechanics’ probabilistic nature has puzzled researchers for more than a century.

A new analysis shows that ridding the theory of this odd characteristic may be even harder than anticipated. Left undisturbed and isolated, the cat remains mixed, but if it is observed – if an experimenter opens its box, say – it abruptly reduces to just one, unmixed state. news.title: AI refutes 30-year-old mathematical assumption in computer science
paras: “This came as a complete surprise, a shock,” says Fedor Fomin at the University of Bergen in Norway. Proposed nearly 30 years ago, the exponential time hypothesis (ETH) tries to put a limit on how quickly computers can solve certain logical puzzles.

The simplest way would be to try every possible combination of true or false for each part of the puzzle. ETH proposes that, although it may be possible to do this quicker with shortcuts, the amount of work needed has to grow exponentially as the puzzle gets bigger.

news.title: How age checks might work for UK social media ban
paras: Ofcom - the independent organisation that helps make sure television, radio and online services follow UK laws and rules - has now recommended four ways that social media companies could check whether users are old enough. The UK is following other countries where bans are in place, including Australia where a similar ban was introduced in December 2025.

However, some children there have found ways around the restrictions , so the UK government says its age checks should be tougher. Published 15 April How could the age checks work? Photo ID matching would check information on an official document, such as a passport.

news.title: Nintendo games designer to get Japanese honour
paras: The legendary games designer behind Mario , Legend of Zelda , and many other famous video games, will be given a very important honour in Japan next week. Shigeru Miyamoto will be presented with the Japanese Order of Culture by the country's Emperor on 3 November, in recognition of his work.

It's a big deal, as not only is it the highest honour of this kind Japan can give out, but Miyamoto will be the first ever games designer to receive it. He said he feels "incredibly awkward but truly honoured" to win the award.

news.title: How do you feel about people smoking on the sidelines when you're playing sport?
paras: Figure caption, Gracie wants to see a ban on adults smoking and vaping on sports sidelines Have you ever noticed spectators smoking or vaping on the sideline when you're playing sport?

If so, how does it make you feel? While indoor public spaces and shared communal areas must be smoke-free, it's not normally against the law to smoke or vape at sports matches if they're outside. Gracie plays for a youth girls team in Cheshire and has been campaigning for a change in the law to ban smoking and vaping at sports matches when children are playing.

news.title: Dinosaur named after fossil-loving dad from Surrey
paras: A new species of dinosaur has been named after a dad who worked in the building where it was found in Surrey, in the south of England. William Proudlove was a manager of the Ewhurst brick and tile works, and was very interested in fossils himself.

An ancient dino fossil was found there in 2001 and donated to the Natural History Museum, who have recently looked at the fossil again and realised it's actually a brand new species. They have now named it Paludohadros proudlovii - a type of iguanodontian, which were plant-eating dinosaurs known for having big spikes on their thumbs.

news.title: Clean-up underway as tens of thousands of homes left without power after Storm Boelo
paras: Storm Boelo battered parts of the north of England, Northern Ireland and Scotland this weekend, and as of 7pm on Sunday night, 90,000 homes were still without power according to the Energy Network Agency. Winds of 85mph were recorded on Saturday, and the high winds caused lots of damage in affected areas.

Published 1 September Boelo came soon after Storm Austen brought strong winds and heavy rain on Friday, leaving many homes in the South West of England without power. An amber warning for wind was in place for Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and parts of northern England on Saturday and Sunday.

80-year-old President Lula da Silva won the election in a surprise victory, with just over half of the vote - 51.79%. He had been trailing behind Mr Bolsonaro after the first round of voting. news.title: 'I didn't know our great-grandma did such amazing things'
paras: Well, Press Packers Elise and Renae's great-grandmother Locita Brandy has won a Manchester University Medal of Honour. She was one of the founders of the Manchester Caribbean Carnival and also fought against racism in education.

The award is for her community work and for many years campaigning to help black children. The sisters went to interview Locita for Newsround to find out more about her life and how she improved things for many black children. They discovered some of her achievements, like changing school dinners, leading Saturday school so kids from the Caribbean could learn about their heritage, and getting books with racist language removed from the school library.

news.title: Young athlete and former minister among victims of Spain train crash
paras: A 24-year-old athlete and a former government minister are among the victims of a deadly train crash that killed 69 people near Urda in central Spain on Wednesday morning. The crash, between a high-speed Renfe train and a stationary Iryo train on the same track, also injured more than 100 people injured, many seriously.

The impact caused carriages to derail, and there are fears the death toll could still rise, with reports of family members searching for missing relatives in hospitals across the region. The bodies of those killed have been taken to the main forensics institute in Toledo, where families have been giving DNA samples to help identify them.

news.title: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
paras: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has laid out her vision for what an "associate membership" status for Canada to the EU would look like as officials gather in Montreal to discuss closer ties. It is "a partnership that comes close to membership than anything we have done before," she said on Thursday's remarks at the two-day Canada-EU summit.

She added it is a type of relationship that would be open "only to our closest partners outside of Europe who are ready to open a new frontier together." It includes close alignment on governance and policies, and partnering in research and innovation.

news.title: Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering
paras: A record 33 members have been expelled from China's Communist Party as it concluded a major annual political gathering, which had the most empty seats ever seen. The fifth plenum was attended by 279 Central Committee members, compared to 315 at the fourth plenum in October 2025 and 364 at the third one in July 2024.

While recent plenums focused on economic reforms or social and development issues, party discipline took centre stage at this week's gathering. Xi Jinping has made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his rule since he took the reins in 2012, calling it the "biggest threat" to the party.

news.title: Building boom puts 300,000 people in the path of potential Himalayan disasters
paras: At least 300,000 people in parts of the Himalayan region could now be living in the path of potential disasters, a new study suggests. Researchers found that the amount of built-up land in high-risk zones in northern Nepal, parts of south-eastern Tibet and a corner of India's Uttarakhand had grown by about 45% between 2016 and 2023.

In areas particularly threatened by flooding from glacial lakes, development increased even faster, rising by almost 78% over the same period, according to the peer-reviewed study published in Scientific Reports. The team of scientists behind it said the true number of people under threat could be much higher, as they only analysed a specific territory and not neighbouring areas which face similar risks.

Rublev has won more than 60% of his matches this season, which includes a title in Bastad and reached another two finals. Those hardly sound like the results of a player experiencing a complete collapse but when compared with his best years, the differences become rather difficult to ignore.
